transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um... the clinic told me I had to come. They've been getting on me about... how little I've been eating, I guess. 

But... I don't know, most days I just grab a coffee before my shift at the warehouse. Maybe a yogurt or a few bites of something after my GED class. Sitting down for an actual meal just... it feels like it throws off everything I'm trying to keep in line. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Do you ever feel a strong fear about gaining weight or feel like you need to do something to keep your weight down, even if you’re already at a low weight?

Um... I guess so. Sometimes. 

Like, if I end up eating something heavy... maybe someone brings fried food into the break room at work, or... or if I eat a bigger plate at a church thing... I just... I get this feeling. Like it's going to show up on me right away. 

I don't know, it just gets stuck in my head. I can't stop thinking about it until I... until I check the scale. Just to be sure.

After eating something you feel is heavy or more than you planned, do you ever try to compensate for it by doing things like exercising a lot, making yourself vomit, or taking laxatives or diet pills?

Um... no. I don't do any of that. 

I don't... make myself sick or take pills or anything. I just... I don't know, I just deal with it.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently, or do you feel that your weight is already too low but still worry about eating more?

I mean... I guess I've lost some. My work pants are pretty loose now. And... people tell me I look too thin. 

But I don't feel like it's too low. When I see the number go down, it just... it feels like I'm finally getting somewhere. I don't really see why I should be pushed to put it back on.
Would you say your weight loss has been something you're trying to achieve, and do you feel like your body weight or shape is influencing how you see yourself overall?

I guess I am trying to lose it, yeah. 

Um... as for how I see myself... I don't know. I mean, when I look in the mirror before... before softball or whatever, I still see that my stomach and my thighs look... bigger than they should. 

And, um... if I feel like they look okay, I feel like I'm doing good. But if they don't... it kind of just makes me feel like I'm failing for the whole day.
Can you tell me more about your efforts to lose weight? Have you set a specific goal for how much you want to weigh or how your body should look, and how have you been trying to reach that goal?

I don't know if I have a... specific number in mind. I just... I just want to feel okay. 

I've just been... watching what I eat, mostly. Keeping track. That's about it.
Have you been restricting your food intake in a way that's different from just watching what you eat, like skipping meals or eating very small amounts on purpose?

I mean... the clinic is the one who got on me about how little I've been eating. But... I don't know. 

Most days I just grab a coffee before I head to the warehouse. And then... maybe a yogurt or just a few bites of something after my GED class. It's just... if I sit down for an actual, real meal, it feels like it throws off everything I'm trying to keep in line. So... yeah. I guess I keep it small.
Have you intentionally limited how much you eat or set strict rules for yourself about what or when you can eat?
I don't really have strict rules, I don't think. I just... try not to eat too much. Like I said, I just keep it small. I don't know what else to say about it.
Would you say that how you see your body — like your stomach or thighs — affects how you feel about yourself overall?

I guess so. Yeah. 

Like... if I'm getting ready for class or, you know, my softball league... and I look in the mirror. I just... my stomach and thighs, they just always look bigger than they should be. And... I don't know. It just kinda decides if I'm doing okay or if I'm... failing, I guess. For the rest of the day.
Can you tell me approximately how much you weigh now, and whether you know what a healthy weight would be for someone your height and age?

I... I'd rather not say the exact number right now. I know what the clinic says is supposed to be healthy for me, but... I don't know. 

I mean, my work pants are loose, and people at the warehouse keep telling me I look too thin. But... when I see that number go down, it just feels like I'm finally getting somewhere. I don't really see why I should be pushed to put it back on.
Have you intentionally tried to lose weight, and if so, how long have you been trying to keep your weight low or lose more weight?

I... I guess I have been. Trying to lose it, I mean. 

Um... I don't really remember exactly when I started. It's just been a while. Maybe a few years? I don't know. It just kind of... became normal for me to try and keep it down.
Have you ever tried to stop yourself from losing more weight, or do you feel like losing weight is something you need to keep doing, even if others are worried about how thin you've become?

I haven't really tried to stop. 

I mean... I know the doctor here and some people from my church say they're worried. But... I honestly think they're just making a bigger deal out of it than it is. I'm still going to work every day. Doing my classes... keeping up with my life just fine. 

So... yeah. I don't really see the problem.
Would you say that your concern about your body shape or weight has become more important to you than other areas of your life, like school, work, or relationships?

I... I wouldn't say it's more important. I'm still showing up for work at the warehouse. And going to my GED classes. 

I guess... maybe I don't go out to eat after church anymore. I just... prefer to stick to my own schedule with food. And sometimes I don't finish my homework because I'm... busy keeping track of things. But I'm still doing what I need to do.
Would you say that you are intentionally keeping your weight below what is considered normal for your height and age, even if others are concerned about your weight loss?

I guess... yes. 

I mean, my work pants are pretty loose now. And people keep saying I look too thin. But... when I step on the scale and see the number go down, it just feels like... like I'm actually getting somewhere. 

I don't really see why everyone is pushing me to put the weight back on. I'm fine where I am.
